nomenclature.etymology_html:
-Mitragyna : From the Greek mitra "a turban, bishop's head-dress" and gyne "a woman, female organ", referring to the stigma and to the cap-shaped ovary.
-Parvifolia : From the Latin parus, parvi- "small" and florus -a -um "flower", small-flowered.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Mitragyna parvifolia is pale grey-coloured, smooth with circular and shallow pits where old bark has flaked off.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Mitragyna parvifolia is pale grey-coloured, smooth with circular and shallow pits where old bark has flaked off.

seed.text: The seeds of Mitragyna parvifolia are flat, spherical and less than 1 mm in diameter.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Mitragyna parvifolia are flat, spherical and less than 1 mm in diameter.

fruit.text: The fruit of Mitragyna parvifolia is a capsule. All the capsules are aggregated into a globular and dense head/infructescence (1 cm in diameter). The capsules are 1.5-2 mm long.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Mitragyna parvifolia is a capsule. All the capsules are aggregated into a globular and dense head/infructescence (1 cm in diameter). The capsules are 1.5-2 mm long.

flower.text: The flowers of Mitragyna parvifolia are grouped in dense, axillary or terminal and globose heads (0.8-1.5 cm across). The calyx is truncate. The calyx-lobes are minute and ciliate. The corolla is cream-coloured. The corolla-tube is 5 mm long. The corolla is 5-lobed. The lobes are 2.5 mm long and recurved. The androecium is composed of 5 stamens attached near the corolla throat. The filament are 3 mm long and the anthers are oblong. The style is filiform and 5 mm long. The ovary is obconic, 1.5 mm long and 2-celled. The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Mitragyna parvifolia are grouped in dense, axillary or terminal and globose heads (0.8-1.5 cm across).
The calyx is truncate. The calyx-lobes are minute and ciliate.
The corolla is cream-coloured. The corolla-tube is 5 mm long. The corolla is 5-lobed. The lobes are 2.5 mm long and recurved.
The androecium is composed of 5 stamens attached near the corolla throat. The filament are 3 mm long and the anthers are oblong.
The style is filiform and 5 mm long.
The ovary is obconic, 1.5 mm long and 2-celled.
The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Mitragyna parvifolia grow opposite on the stem. The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is glabrous on both sides (some minute hairs on the midrib beneath). The leaves have a 1-1.5 cm long petiole . The leaf of Mitragyna parvifolia is 7-11 cm long and 4-6 cm wide. The shape of the blade is ovate to oblong, the apex is obtuse, the base is rounded and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.
leaf.text_html:

The leaves have a 1-1.5 cm long petiole.

The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Mitragyna parvifolia is a large deciduous tree with a short and irregular trunk and a spreading crown. Mitragyna parvifolia can grows up to 25-30 m high.
habit.text_html:
Mitragyna parvifolia is a large deciduous tree with a short and irregular trunk and a spreading crown.
Mitragyna parvifolia can grows up to 25-30 m high.

ecology.text: Mitragyna parvifolia is found in deciduous forests, ravine areas and along river banks from the coastal plains up to 900-1000 m high in the hills.
ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Mitragyna parvifolia is found in deciduous forests, ravine areas and along river banks from the coastal plains up to 900-1000 m high in the hills.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Mitragyna parvifolia is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Mitragyna parvifolia is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Mitragyna parvifolia are dispersed by the wind (anemochory).
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Mitragyna parvifolia is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Mitragyna parvifolia is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Mitragyna parvifolia are dispersed by the wind (anemochory).

phenology.text: From February to June. Throughout the year (the fruits are persistent). Throughout the year. During the hot season. ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )

handicrafts.text: The wood of Mitragyna parvifolia is hard and durable if not exposed. It takes a good polish. The wood is used in building construction (planks and rafters), for making furniture, agricultural implements, small articles and for turning. A fibre from the bark is used to make cordage. Source : Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan
handicrafts.text_html:
The wood of Mitragyna parvifolia is hard and durable if not exposed. It takes a good polish. The wood is used in building construction (planks and rafters), for making furniture, agricultural implements, small articles and for turning.

A fibre from the bark is used to make cordage.

Source : Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan

medicinal.text: The roots , bark and the leaves of Mitragyna parvifolia are used in internal and external haemorrhages, skin diseases, leprosy and fever. ( Arya Vaidya Sala, 1996, Indian Medicinal plants ) The leaf paste is applied on wounds. The pounded leaves with garlic are used to treat chronic cough. The leaf juice is used as hepatic stimulant, hepatoprotective, to cure jaundice and for liver ailments. The bark paste and juice are applied for muscular pains and dog bite. Source : Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants

reforestation.text: Mitragyna parvifolia is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils. The species is propagated by seeds. No pre-treatment is required. Mitragyna parvifolia seeds need heat and light to germinate, so they need to be sown on the top of the soil with nothing covering them.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Mitragyna parvifolia is a light demander and fairly drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    No pre-treatment is required.
    Mitragyna parvifolia seeds need heat and light to germinate, so they need to be sown on the top of the soil with nothing covering them.
